latest_release.name: DuckDB v2.0.1 Bugfix Release
latest_release.body:
This is a bug fix release for various issues discovered after we released v2.0.0.

Please also refer to the announcement blog post: https://duckdb.org/2026/11/20/announcing-duckdb-201.html

## What's Changed
* Merge Rust extension CI groups by @smvv in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27600
* Print the profiler's trailing blank line through the renderer's print sink by @h4nsmuller in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27604
* Fix StagedUpload.yml by @lnkuiper in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27610
* Fix StagedUpload.yml by @lnkuiper in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27612
* Run more release checks on non-main branch by @smvv in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27548
* Fix appending chunks larger than the vector size that need a cast by @iremcaginyurtturk in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27665
* Backport labeled fixes to v2.0-cyanoptera by @smvv in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27684
* Compare ANY and ALL of ARRAY(SELECT ...) against the elements of the list by @Robinho-MR in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27781
* Parquet writer: keep a column's min/max in RETURN_STATS when a row group holds only NULLs for it by @h4nsmuller in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27875
* Add casts from TIMESTAMPTZ_NS to TIMESTAMP by @kdmodii in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27928
* Add a parquet_can_have_nan setting as the default for the can_have_nan option by @kdmodii in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27969
* [v2.0-cyanoptera] Backport labeled fixes through #27935 by @smvv in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27965
* [AUTOMATED_EDIT] Add v2.0.1 to version_map.json by @maiadegraaf in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28020
* [v2.0-cyanoptera] Backport merged labeled fixes by @Robinho-MR in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28072
* Treat error() as non-volatile when deciding duplicate elimination in decorrelation by @EtgarDev in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28125
* Cyanoptera revert unmerged by @carlopi in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28247
* [v2.0-cyanoptera] Backport #28129: free a segment's buffer once its data is copied into a partial block by @ywelsch in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28139
* [v2.0-cyanoptera] Backport merged labeled fixes (2) by @Robinho-MR in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28290
* Keep the incoming join order as a candidate in greedy join ordering by @DinosL in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28362
* [v2.0-cyanoptera] Backport merged labeled fixes (3) by @Robinho-MR in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28396
* Link Wasm extensions against vcpkg_installed/${VCPKG_TARGET_TRIPLET}, on cyanoptera by @carlopi in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28545
* Bump aws to c2f2568 (name + resolve callbacks for both resource types), on cyanoptera by @carlopi in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28519
* [Testing] Fix problems with error logging for certain error paths by @Tishj in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28577
* [v2.0-cyanoptera] Backport #27943: size partitioned COPY batches from the written columns by @Robinho-MR in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28589
* Look up the columns of a multi-file scan by name through an index when reading their statistics by @h4nsmuller in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28638
* Update Postgres, MySQL and SQLite (2.0.1) by @staticlibs in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28575
* [v2.0-cyanoptera] Bump avro to b7b157f50dd0 by @autograaf in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28657
* [v2.0-cyanoptera] Backport merged labeled fixes (4) by @Robinho-MR in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28602
* Backport 28373 28427 by @Tmonster in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28733
* bump iceberg and glue by @Tmonster in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28459
* [v2.0-cyanoptera] Bump spatial by @autograaf in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28644
* chore: pin delta, unity_catalog and azure for the v2.0.1 patch

detail.readme: ## DuckDB DuckDB is a high-performance analytical database system. It is designed to be fast, reliable, portable, and easy to use. DuckDB runs in-process inside your application, so there is no separate server to manage and no external dependencies. It can also read remote files, query other databases, and connect to other DuckDB instances when needed. It provides a rich SQL dialect with support far beyond basic SQL: arbitrary and nested correlated subqueries, window functions, collations, and complex types (arrays, structs, maps). Its [friendly SQL](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/sql/dialect/friendly_sql.html) extensions add syntax that makes queries shorter and easier to write. DuckDB is available as a [standalone CLI application](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/clients/cli/overview) and has clients for [Python](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/clients/python/overview), [R](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/clients/r), [Java](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/clients/java), [Rust](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/clients/rust), [Go](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/clients/go), [Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/clients/wasm/overview), and [many more](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/clients/overview), with deep integrations with packages such as [pandas](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/guides/python/sql_on_pandas). For more information on using DuckDB, please refer to the [DuckDB documentation](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/). ## Reads and writes any data DuckDB reads and writes a wide range of file formats, including [CSV](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/data/csv/overview), [Parquet](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/data/parquet/overview), [JSON](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/data/json/overview), and [Excel](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/excel), directly from local disk or from remote endpoints such as S3, HTTP(S), Azure, and Google Cloud Storage. For many of these formats, including CSV, Parquet, and JSON, loading data is as simple as referencing the file in the FROM clause: ```sql SELECT * FROM 'myfile.csv'; SELECT * FROM 'myfile.parquet'; ``` DuckDB also works with open lakehouse formats. [DuckLake](https://ducklake.select/) stores table metadata in a SQL database rather than in metadata files, which removes the need for a separate catalog server while still providing ACID transactions, snapshots, and time travel. DuckDB also supports the [Apache Iceberg](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/iceberg/overview) and [Delta Lake](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/delta) formats. Refer to our [Data Import](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/data/overview) section for more information. ## Connects to other databases DuckDB can attach to other database systems and query them in place, so you can read, join, and move data across engines without a separate ETL step. It speaks the native protocols of [PostgreSQL](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/postgres/overview), [MySQL](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/mysql), and [SQLite](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/sqlite). DuckDB instances can also connect to each other over the [quack protocol](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/quack/overview), which turns a DuckDB instance into a server that other DuckDB clients attach to over HTTP. ## Extensible DuckDB has a modular [extension mechanism](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/extensions/overview): core extensions are bundled with DuckDB, while community and third-party extensions can be installed and loaded at runtime. Extensions add file formats, database connectors, and new functions, types, and more. ## Installation If you want to install DuckDB, please see [our installation page](https://duckdb.org/docs/installation/) for instructions. ## SQL Reference The documentation contains a [SQL introduction and reference](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/sql/introduction). ## Development For development, DuckDB requires [CMake](https://cmake.org), Python 3 and a `C++17` compliant compiler. In the root directory, run `make` to compile the sources. For development, use `make debug` to build a non-optimized debug version. You should run `make unit` and `make allunit` to verify that your version works properly after making changes. To test performance, you can run `BUILD_BENCHMARK=1 BUILD_TPCH=1 make` and then perform several standard benchmarks from the root directory by executing `./build/release/benchmark/benchmark_runner`. The details of benchmarks are in our [Benchmark Guide](benchmark/README.md). Please also refer to our [Build Guide](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/dev/building/overview) and [Contribution Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Support See the [Support Options](https://ducklabs.com/support/) page and the dedicated [`endoflife.date`](https://endoflife.date/duckdb) page.
